body.p: Once upon a time there was a hare. It got cold. The hare went out of his yurt. He found a man - a frozen human being. |||| He walked round the dead person. And he sees a fox coming. The fox came and said: 'What are you doing here, hare?' 'I found a human being! How can we eat a frozen person?' The fox says to the hare: 'Go this way!' An old man and an old woman live there - ask for a hammer and chisel, ask for it!' The hare went away. He walked and walked and walked, long or short, he reached the yurt. He entered the yurt. 'Old man and old woman,' he said, 'I've come! Give me a hammer and a chisel!' 'Why do you need a hammer? Why do you need a chisel?' 'I found a frozen person!' 'Eh, you want to eat my son!' The old man wanted to hit the hare with the hook [for hanging kettles] - the hare jumped out. He hit the hare in the || doorway with the hook. He hit the hare's tail, his tail broke, his tail became short.[StN]: irgilin kapurɣaran -- why not NOM? The hare went, he went back. He came to this human being. The fox ate everything [this frozen man], the fox. Then the hare went, he began to sing and went: 'Am I going high or am I going low!?'[StN]: Čatildoti, Korboldoti - ((unknown)) The hare saw: a fire was burning; a stump [was burning].[StN]: čalə - cvb.ant? Again, he sang: 'Am I going high or am I going low?'[StN]: čatildati, korboldoti - ((unknown)) Two girls were sitting spinning thread.[StN]: -l in prʼadildʼara - ?? The hare said: 'Why are you [StN]: 2PL -š (not -šun) ==> AOR (not PST)sitting here? Go and pour water on the fire!'[StN]: number mismatch: imperative 2SG ... 2PL The hare went further. Two mice are running under the bottom. 'Why are you mice running around here? Go to the girls and cut their threads!'[StN]: 1) valency pattern "go + ACC"? 2) NB -wÉl as a suffix (before case markers) The hare went on. He walked and walked and walked [sees]: two boys shooting from a bow.' 'Who are you shooting at, two boys?[StN]: ewaduk - nonstandard meaning of ABL Shoot those two mice [StN]: tarwoldu - -wəl is used as a suffixunder the bottom!' The hare went on. He walked and walked and walked - he reached a grassy swamp. He ran through this swamp and cut his nose crosswise with grass.[StN]: хоˊһ - һ>g? krestakakčan - ((unknown)) (maybe креˊsтика-кчан, kakčan as a separate word with no clear meaning is once attested in Corpus) He returned home - he came home. He wanted to open the door, but a frog was sitting in the yurt.[StN]: mulə=DESID? He said: 'snowdrop anemone la-la-la-la-la-la-la-la, I'll eat a hare!Растеніе (Anemone sіlvеstris L) — употр. отъ грыжи. Snowdrop anemone mol-mol-mol, I'll eat the hare!' The hare was frightened. The hare left. He walked and walked and met a bear and said, 'Grandfather, in the yurt,' he said, 'who is that saying? [StN]: ACC -wi ((unknown))Snowdrop anemone mol-mol-mol, snowdrop anemone la-la-la-la-la!' He's going || to eat me! Grandfather, let's go into the yurt!' The hare goes with the grandfather [bear] into the yurt.[StN]: come - 3sg; house - why 3sg, not refl?The grandfather opened the yurt, came in and said: 'There is no one!'[StN]: amakan - n-final = stem or poss? The hare says: 'Take a good look!'[StN]: -či - a variant of -t or a separate entry? The bear looked: there was a frog sitting on the edge of the pole.[StN]: šarəŋil = tent-place's (poles) -? The bear hit [the frog] with the palm of his hand and killed it. From then on, the hare lived in his yurt.[StN]: AND in the inchoative use? The bear left.
